advisory: A finding aid for how a day is put together, and never an authority for what was celebrated. The rules here are transcribed from this repository's own collated publications; the competent particular calendar, a legitimate indult and the competent annual Ordo control an actual celebration. Precedence is one of five decisions, and this layer takes only that one and the orations that follow from it.

bases.why: the vigil of the Nativity, a first-class vigil, or its octave day

bases.label: a first-class Sunday
bases.why: a first-class Sunday - one of the four of Advent, the four of Lent, the two of Passiontide, or Low Sunday

bases.label: a first-class feria
bases.why: a first-class feria: Ash Wednesday, or Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday of Holy Week, which take precedence over any feast whatever

bases.why: the Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed

bases.why: the vigil of Pentecost, a first-class vigil which yields to nothing and admits no commemoration

bases.why: a day within the octave of Easter or of Pentecost, which are first-class octaves

bases.label: a first-class feast of the universal calendar
bases.why: a first-class feast of the universal Church not named in the rows above

bases.label: a second-class feast of the Lord
bases.why: a second-class feast of the Lord, which takes the place of a second-class Sunday it meets

bases.label: a second-class Sunday
bases.why: a second-class Sunday - every Sunday that is not one of the six first-class kinds

bases.label: a second-class feast of the universal calendar
bases.why: a second-class feast of the universal Church which is not of the Lord

bases.label: a day within the octave of the Nativity
bases.why: a day within the octave of the Nativity, a second-class octave

bases.label: a second-class feria
bases.why: a second-class feria: an Advent feria from 17 to 23 December, or an Ember Day of Advent, Lent or September. It must be commemorated if impeded

bases.label: a second-class vigil
bases.why: one of the four second-class vigils: the Ascension, the Assumption, the Nativity of St John the Baptist, and Ss Peter and Paul. Commemorated if impeded, but dropped entirely on a Sunday or a first-class feast

bases.label: a feria of Lent or Passiontide
bases.why: a feria of Lent or Passiontide outside the Ember Days, which takes precedence over third-class feasts and must be commemorated if impeded

bases.label: a third-class feast of the universal calendar
bases.why: a third-class feast inscribed in the calendar of the universal Church

bases.label: a feria of Advent before 17 December
bases.why: an Advent feria to 16 December outside the Ember Days, which yields to third-class feasts and must be commemorated if impeded

bases.label: the vigil of St Lawrence
bases.why: the one third-class vigil, that of St Lawrence

bases.label: the Office of Our Lady on Saturday
bases.why: the Office of Our Lady on Saturday, kept on a Saturday that carries a fourth-class feria. It is an Office and not a feast, and any occurring feast displaces it

bases.label: a fourth-class feria
bases.why: a fourth-class feria: every feria not named above. It is never commemorated

bases.label: a commemoration inscribed in the calendar
bases.locus: RG 91 (the table has no row for a commemoration); RG 107-108
bases.why: an entry the calendar inscribes as a commemoration and not as a feast. It occupies no row of the table, so it can never take the day; it can only ever be an ordinary commemoration

bases.label: a further Mass appointed on this day
bases.locus: the Missal prints both formularies at this day
bases.why: a further Mass the Missal appoints on a day whose identity is settled elsewhere. It is not a competitor for the day

bases.label: a formulary the Missal prints for a slot another day occupies
bases.locus: RG 17; the Missal's own heading at the formulary
bases.why: a formulary the Missal prints for a slot another celebration occupies. It is a formulary, not a liturgical day, and it competes for nothing

code: Codex rubricarum, 25 July 1960, as printed in the 1962 Missale Romanum

abolished.locus: Variationes cap. II n. 13; cap. IV n. 18 (Acta 52 (1960) 708-709)
abolished.what: The Suffragium de omnibus Sanctis, the commemoratio de Cruce and the seasonal second and third orations of Advent, Lent and the Sundays - the orationes pro diversitate Temporum that older hand missals print beneath the collect - were abolished with the code. A reader holding a pre-1955 hand missal is holding a book whose commemoration apparatus has been dismantled, not trimmed, and its printed second and third collects must not be used with the 1962 calendar.

ceilings.latin: Ratio admittendi commemorationes haec est: a) in diebus liturgicis I classis et in Missis in cantu non conventualibus, nulla admittitur commemoratio, praeter unam privilegiatam; b) in dominicis II classis, una tantum admittitur commemoratio, scilicet de festo II classis, quae tamen omittitur si commemoratio privilegiata facienda sit; c) in aliis diebus liturgicis II classis, una tantum admittitur commemoratio, scilicet aut una privilegiata aut una ordinaria; d) in diebus liturgicis III et IV classis, duae tantum admittuntur commemorationes.

rules.what: On a first-class day, one commemoration only and it must be privileged.
On a second-class Sunday, one commemoration only, and it must be of a second-class feast; it is omitted if a privileged commemoration is due, and that privileged one is made instead.
On any other second-class day, exactly one commemoration, privileged or ordinary.
On a third- or fourth-class day, two commemorations.

sung_non_conventual.what: A sung Mass that is not the conventual Mass is put in the same clause as a first-class day: one privileged commemoration and no more, whatever the calendar says. A parish sung Mass on a fourth-class Tuesday therefore has fewer orations than the Low Mass said at the side altar an hour earlier.

list.what: An Office, Mass or commemoration of a feast or mystery of one divine Person excludes a commemoration or prayer of another feast or mystery of the same Person.
An Office, Mass or commemoration of the Sunday excludes a commemoration or prayer of a feast or mystery of the Lord, and conversely.
An Office, Mass or commemoration de Tempore excludes another commemoration de Tempore.

An Office, Mass or commemoration of Our Lady or of a saint excludes another commemoration or prayer asking the same intercession - but not the prayer of the Sunday or feria in which the same saint is invoked.

exclusions.not_applied_note: Clauses a and d turn on the identity of a divine Person or of a saint, which this file cannot read off a mass key. They are stated at the step where they would apply and are never applied. Where either might bite, the page says the case is unsettled here.

inseparable.what: The mutual commemoration of Ss Peter and Paul is inseparable: in the Office or Mass of either, the other's prayer is added under a single conclusion, and "duae orationes adeo in unam coalescere censentur ut, in numero orationum computando, pro unica habeantur". Two prayers counting as one.

kinds.gloss: An ordinary commemoration is made at every Low Mass and at the conventual Mass, and at no other sung Mass. A sung parish Mass that is not a conventual Mass drops every ordinary commemoration, whatever the day. This is the single most-missed rule in the apparatus.
kinds.latin: Commemorationes sunt aut privilegiatae aut ordinariae. Commemorationes privilegiatae fiunt in Laudibus et in Vesperis necnon in omnibus Missis; commemorationes vero ordinariae fiunt tantum in Laudibus, in Missis conventualibus et in omnibus Missis lectis.

order.gloss: The season first, then the table order.
order.latin: Commemoratio de Tempore fit primo loco. In admittendis et ordinandis aliis commemorationibus, servetur ordo tabellae praecedentiae.

privileged.closing: Omnes aliae commemorationes sunt commemorationes ordinariae.

divergences.publication_reads: from the Thursday after Ash Wednesday to the Saturday before Passion Sunday inclusive
divergences.this_file_reads: from the Thursday after Ash Wednesday to the Saturday before Palm Sunday inclusive
divergences.what: the span of the third-class ferias at row 22
divergences.why: The publication's own Case 1a classes Wednesday 17 March 2027 - a weekday of Passion week, after Passion Sunday - at row 22 and states the span as running "to the Saturday before Palm Sunday (20 March) inclusive". Its transcription of the row and of RG 25 a says "Passion Sunday" instead. The tracked 1962 calendar in this repository independently prints rank III against every feria of Passion week, and RG 23 makes Monday to Wednesday of Holy Week first class, which leaves no other class for the days between. This file follows the case and the calendar, records the disagreement, and does not claim to have resolved it against the witness.

fixed_commemoration.gloss: A commemoration attached to a date does not travel with the feast it accompanies.
fixed_commemoration.latin: Commemoratio die fixo statuta non transfertur vel reponitur cum festo transferendo vel reponendo, sed fit suo die vel omittitur.

reposition.why: Reposition answers a perpetual collision, which is a permanent fact about a particular calendar rather than a fact about a date. This repository carries no particular calendar, so nothing here is ever repositioned.

sunday_not_resumed.gloss: An impeded Sunday is gone for that year. It is not moved forward, back, or into the following week.
sunday_not_resumed.latin: Officium et Missa dominicae impeditae nec anticipantur nec resumuntur.

destination.rule: the next following day that is neither first nor second class
destination.why_not: The destination depends on the class of every following day and on RG 97-98, which order several transferred feasts among themselves. This repository does not compute it, and a page that guessed it would be asserting an Ordo result it has not checked. The two destinations the rubric fixes by name are computed, because the rubric states them.

keeps_its_class.latin: Festa translata sunt eiusdem gradus ac in sede propria.

transfer.latin: Ius translationis in alium diem ob occurrentiam accidentalem cum die liturgico, qui in tabella praecedentiae superiorem obtinet locum, competit solummodo festis I classis. Alia festa, ab Officio gradus superioris accidentaliter impedita, aut commemorantur aut, eo anno, penitus omittuntur, iuxta rubricas.
transfer.proper_seat_note: "Tamquam in sedem propriam" matters: a day reached as a proper seat is not a borrowed lodging. On it the transferred item behaves as though it were at home, and the third-class feast that ordinarily occupies that date is impeded for that year.

proper_seats.latin: festum Annuntiationis B. Mariae Virg., quando est transferendum post Pascha, transfertur, tamquam in sedem propriam, in feriam II post dominicam in albis
proper_seats.when: 25 March falls between Palm Sunday and the Saturday after Easter inclusive, which is when it must be transferred past Easter

proper_seats.latin: Commemoratio omnium Fidelium defunctorum, quando occurrit cum dominica, transfertur, tamquam in sedem propriam, in feriam II sequentem

vigil_dropped.gloss: A second- or third-class vigil is dropped altogether - penitus omittitur - if it falls on a Sunday or on a first-class feast, or if the feast it precedes is itself transferred or reduced to a commemoration.

implied.label: a feria of Advent from 17 to 23 December
implied.note: An Advent Ember Day falling in this window is also a second-class feria, so the row holds either way.

implied.label: a feria of Advent before 17 December
implied.note: The Ember Days of Advent follow the Third Sunday of Advent, which is the First Sunday plus fourteen days, so the earliest of them is that Sunday's Wednesday - the First Sunday plus seventeen. A weekday before it cannot be an Ember Day, and the row is therefore settled without dating them. The bound is the reasoning the publication's own Case 1b performs by hand.

implied.label: a feria of Advent before 17 December
implied.unless: the day is one of the three Ember Days of Advent, which are second-class ferias at row 18 (RG 24 b) and would take the day from a third-class feast rather than yield to it. guidance/liturgy/calendar-computation.md does not date the Advent Ember Days, so this repository cannot exclude them once the Third Sunday of Advent has passed.

implied.label: a day within the octave of the Nativity
a feria after the Epiphany
implied.note: RG 64 celebrates only the octaves of Christmas, Easter and Pentecost, so the days after the Epiphany are ordinary ferias.

implied.label: a feria of Paschaltide
implied.note: The Greater Litanies and the Rogation days fall in this season and are not dated here. They do not change the feria's class; what is lost is the privileged commemoration of RG 109 f, which is recorded under `unsettled`.

implied.label: a feria after Pentecost, in September
implied.unless: the day is one of the three Ember Days of September, which are second-class ferias at row 18 (RG 24 b). guidance/liturgy/calendar-computation.md does not date the September Ember Days, so this repository cannot exclude them from a September weekday.

known_absences.effect: A first-class feast of the Lord at row 3 would take this day from any Sunday after Pentecost. It is absent from this calendar index, so the winner shown below is not the day's identity.
known_absences.when: the last Sunday of October, which always falls between 25 and 31 October

known_absences.effect: RG 17 a assigns the Most Holy Name of Jesus perpetually to this Sunday, where it takes the Sunday's place. It is absent from this calendar index, so this date carries no day at all here. Where no Sunday falls between 2 and 5 January the feast is kept on 2 January, which this file does not date.
known_absences.when: the Sunday falling between 2 and 5 January

mass_category.assumed: the Mass of the Office of the day
mass_category.latin: Missa proinde per se cum Officio diei concordare debet.

not_tested.category: the ordination Mass on Ember Saturdays

mass_category.warning: A day's class tells you only that a category is not excluded. What admits it is a separate fact - about the church, the celebrant, the day's exercises, or an indult - and permission is never inferred from rank.

not_decided_here: Which calendar binds the celebrant (RGMR 274-284), and every particular, diocesan, religious, patronal, titular and dedication feast that calendar carries. Rows 12, 13, 19, 20 and 23 of the table are therefore always empty here, and row 23 outranks row 24.
The Gloria, which depends on whether the Te Deum was said at Matins (RGMR 431; RGBR 237-238, which the Missal does not print).
The Creed (RGMR 475-476), the Preface (RGMR 482-499), the colour (RG 117-132), the Last Gospel (RGMR 509-510) and the tone.
Whether a first-class feast transferred from an earlier date occupies this one, except at the two proper seats RG 96 a-b names.
Concurrence, which disposes of Vespers and never of the next morning's Mass (RG 103-105).

absolute_cap.latin: Quaelibet oratio, quae numerum pro singulis diebus liturgicis statutum superet, omittitur; profecto numerum ternarium orationum nullo praetextu excedere licet.

ceiling_covers_all.what: The ceiling counts all of them together, not only the commemorations.

conclusions.what: The Mass's own oration is said under its own conclusion unless another is joined to it; commemorations, the imposed prayer and the votive prayer are always said under a second conclusion.

imposed_prayer.what: The local Ordinary may impose one prayer for a grave and public necessity. It is barred on every first- and second-class day, in every sung Mass, and whenever privileged commemorations have already filled the day's number. Whether one is imposed is a fact about a diocese, so this page never adds one and never assumes there is none.

prayer_over_the_people.what: Added after the last postcommunion in Masses OF the ferias of Lent and Passiontide, the Sacred Triduum excepted; under its own conclusion; said even when three postcommunions have preceded.

tracked_by.what: as many as there were orations at the beginning of Mass, in the same order and with the same conclusions

votive_prayer.what: Any priest may add one at his discretion in read non-conventual Masses on fourth-class days, placed last. It is a choice, not a rule, so this page never adds one.

what_counts.what: the oration of the Mass being celebrated; the orations of a commemorated Office and of any occurring commemoration; other orations the rubrics prescribe; the prayer imposed by the local Ordinary; and the votive prayer.

overrides.why: All Souls stands at row 8, above the vigil of Pentecost and above every first-class feast of the universal Church, and the row itself adds "quae tamen locum cedit dominicae occurrenti". It is the only qualified row in the table.

In a year whose count of Sundays after Pentecost leaves the numbered Sunday and the last Sunday in one slot, the Mass Dominica XXIV et ultima post Pentecosten is the one that is said: RG 18's closing paragraph puts it last always. Both are second-class Sundays at row 15, so the table alone cannot separate them.

Two feasts of the same divine Person, or of the same saint or blessed, do not commemorate one another: the lower is simply omitted and is not transferred. This file cannot detect that identity from a mass key, so it is stated and never applied.

concurrence.gloss: Concurrence is the meeting of one evening's Vespers, not of two days. It never decides which Mass is said the next morning. That is occurrence, settled by the same table on the following day's own competitors.

effect.gloss: Four outcomes and no others - omission, commemoration, transfer, reposition.
effect.latin: Effectus occurrentiae est, ut Officium diei liturgici gradus inferioris Officio gradus superioris cedat: quod fieri potest per minus nobilis omissionem, aut commemorationem, aut translationem, aut repositionem.

precedence.gloss: Twenty-eight numbered rows, banded into the four classes of day. A lower row number wins. The table ranks days, not saints: eight of its rows contain no feast at all, and a universal third-class feast sits below both the Lenten ferias and any third-class feast a particular calendar owns.
precedence.latin: Praecedentia dierum liturgicorum, sublatis quibuslibet aliis titulis vel normis, unice regitur ex sequenti tabella dierum liturgicorum secundum ordinem praecedentiae disposita.

occurrence.gloss: The distinction selects the remedy. Accidental occurrence may lead to transfer; perpetual occurrence may lead to reposition. A feast cannot be transferred out of a perpetual collision or repositioned out of an accidental one.
occurrence.latin: Occurrentia dicitur occursus duorum vel plurium Officiorum uno eodemque die. Occurrentia autem dicitur accidentalis, quando dies liturgicus mobilis et dies liturgicus fixus certis solummodo annorum intervallis simul occurrunt; perpetua vero quando duo dies liturgici quotannis simul occurrunt.

saturday_office.why: On a Saturday carrying a fourth-class feria the Office is of Our Lady on Saturday. Its Mass exists and may be sung, but any occurring feast displaces it, because row 27 sits below rows 23 and 24.

source_advisory: This file states which rubric governs a decision. It does not state what was celebrated anywhere. Precedence is only one of five decisions, and a day resolved here is still subject to the particular calendar of the church, the place, the diocese and the religious institute, to a legitimate indult, and to the competent annual Ordo, which controls. Nothing here is an occurrence witness and nothing here authorises the use of any book.

unsettled.effect: Row 3 of the table has no mass for Christ the King in this repository, and a Sunday falling between 2 and 5 January carries no day at all. The page says it cannot constitute the day rather than handing it to whatever else the date carries.
unsettled.what: three formularies the Missal carries and this calendar index does not
unsettled.why: The index's own notes record them: D. N. Iesu Christi Regis on the last Sunday of October, Sanctissimi Nominis Iesu on the Sunday between 2 and 5 January, and the Mass for the days within the octave of the Nativity used on 29, 30 and 31 December. None is in the fixed-date spine, so nothing places them.

unsettled.what: two entries that are the same celebration under different keys
unsettled.why: A year with exactly twenty-three Sundays after Pentecost puts the numbered Sunday and the last Sunday in one slot, and the day file emits both. RG 18's closing paragraph decides it and is applied as an override; the underlying duplication is in the day file rather than here.

unsettled.effect: an implied Advent feria before 17 December, and an implied feria after Pentecost, are marked uncertain and the page says the result may not hold.
unsettled.what: the three Ember Days of Advent and the three of September
unsettled.why: guidance/liturgy/calendar-computation.md does not date them, so calendar-days never places them and this file cannot exclude them from an Advent or after-Pentecost weekday.

unsettled.effect: On 25 April a commemoration is derived as ordinary and may in fact be privileged, which changes whether it survives at a sung non-conventual Mass.
unsettled.what: the Greater Litanies and the Rogation days
unsettled.why: The calendar index inscribes the Greater Litanies at 25 April under one key with the feast of St Mark, so where that day loses, this page cannot tell the feast's ordinary commemoration from the Litanies' commemoration, which RG 109 f makes privileged in the Mass. The Rogation Mass itself is not dated in guidance/liturgy/calendar-computation.md and is never placed, so the three Rogation days before the Ascension do not appear at all.

unsettled.what: two candidates that land on the same row
unsettled.why: the table orders within several rows - movable before fixed, proper before indulted - and this repository cannot always tell which a mass is. Where two candidates tie, the derivation stops and says the day is not settled here.

unsettled.what: RG 95 second paragraph, RG 110 and RG 112 a and d
unsettled.why: all four turn on the identity of a divine Person or of a saint, which cannot be read off a mass key. They are stated where they would apply and never applied.
